intro: For a real plan you use «si» + present; for something imagined, «si» + imperfect subjunctive and the conditional.
p.tuviera.consejo: It comes from «tuvieron»: drop «-ron» and add «-ra». It works for yo, él and ella.
p.pudiera.consejo: It comes from «pudieron». After «si» it is used to imagine: «si pudiera, viajaría».
p.fuera.consejo: It works for «ser» and «ir», because in the indefinido both make «fueron».
p.hiciera.consejo: It comes from «hicieron». With the weather: «si hiciera sol». The «h» is silent.
p.viajaría.consejo: The conditional goes in the result: «si pudiera, viajaría». It is regular: «viajar» + «-ía».
p.recorrería.consejo: «Recorrer» is to travel through a whole place. It is regular: «recorrer» + «-ía».
p.si.consejo: Without an accent mark it is the condition: «si pudiera». With one, «sí», it is a yes.
p.a distancia.consejo: Working «a distancia» means doing it from home or somewhere else, over the internet.
p.la posibilidad.consejo: It ends in «-dad» and is feminine: «la posibilidad», like «la verdad».
p.el alojamiento.consejo: It comes from «alojar». A hotel or a country house are alojamientos.
p.la ruta.consejo: It is feminine: «la ruta». The initial «r» sounds strong: «RRU-ta».
p.imaginar.consejo: With «imagina que» + subjunctive you propose a situation: «imagina que tuvieras un año libre».
b1.titulo: A real plan or an imagined one?
b1.texto:
There are two kinds of condition:

- **Real or possible**: **si** + present. The result goes in the present, future or imperative. **Si tengo tiempo, voy / iré / llámame.**
- **Imagined or unlikely**: **si** + imperfect subjunctive. The result goes in the conditional. **Si tuviera tiempo, viajaría más.**

The second one does not say it is impossible: only that you imagine it.

Never put the conditional after **si**: **Si tuviera tiempo, viajaría** (not *si tendría*).
b2.f0.texto: If I could leave work for a year, I would travel around South America.
b2.f1.texto: And what would you do with the flat?
b2.f2.texto: If I rented it out, I would have money for the trip.
b2.f3.texto: If I were in your place, I would talk it through calmly.
b2.f4.texto: If I had more savings, I would leave right now.
b2.f5.texto: If your boss accepted remote work, you could travel without problems.
b2.f6.texto: If everything were that easy, I would already be at the airport.
b2.f7.texto: If you did it, where would you go first?
b4.texto:
- **Si** + present → present, future or imperative: **Si tengo** dinero, **voy** de viaje.
- **Si** + imperfect subjunctive → conditional: **Si tuviera** dinero, **iría** de viaje.

The imperfect subjunctive usually comes from the third person plural of the indefinido: **tuvieron → tuviera**, **hicieron → hiciera**, **fueron → fuera**. The endings are **-ra, -ras, -ra, -ramos, -rais, -ran**. With **nosotros** it has an accent mark: **tuviéramos**, **habláramos**.

The conditional does not go in the **si** part.
b4.e0.texto: If I had time, I would travel more.
b4.e1.texto: If you could, you would help me.
b4.e2.texto: If it were sunny tomorrow, we would go to the beach.
b5.f0.texto: Marta lives in a small flat overlooking a red-brick courtyard.
b5.f1.texto: Every night she spreads a large map on the dining-room table.
b5.f2.texto: With her finger she follows the blue line of a route of slow trains.
b5.f3.texto: If she had six free months, she would travel through those countries without hurry.
b5.f4.texto: For now she only has two weeks of holiday a year.
b5.f5.texto: First she would cross snow-covered mountains on a train with misted-up windows.
b5.f6.texto: Then she would sleep in simple accommodation beside a quiet lake.
b5.f7.texto: Every morning the smell of warm bread would wake her gently.
b5.f8.texto: She would write long letters to her friends from cafés full of unfamiliar voices.
b5.f9.texto: When she got back, the map would be full of marks and coffee stains.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes: imperfect subjunctive after «si», and conditional in the result.
b6.o1.refuerzo: The conditional does not go in the «si» part.
b6.o2.refuerzo: That would describe a real condition, not an imagined one.
b6.pregunta: You imagine having time. Which form is missing?
b7.o0.refuerzo: That's it: «si» + present, and the result in the future.
b7.o1.refuerzo: That is an imagined condition: subjunctive and conditional.
b7.o2.refuerzo: That form is wrong: the conditional is not put after «si».
b7.pregunta: Which is a real or possible condition?
b8.traduccion: If I could, I would travel around South America
b9.o0.refuerzo: The future would go with a real condition, «si tengo tiempo».
b9.o1.refuerzo: Yes: the conditional goes with «si» + subjunctive.
b9.o2.refuerzo: The imperfect does not work as the result of this condition.
b9.pregunta: Which form goes in the result of an imagined wish?
b10.o0.refuerzo: That form does not exist: the conditional of «hacer» is «haría».
b10.o2.refuerzo: That's it: it comes from «hicieron», replacing «-ron» with «-ra».
b10.pregunta: What is the imperfect subjunctive of «hacer»?
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «If I had time»
b12.frase: Si mañana ____ sol, iríamos a la playa.
b12.o0.refuerzo: The conditional does not go after «si».
b12.o1.refuerzo: The present would describe a real condition; here it is imagined.
b12.o2.refuerzo: Well done! Imperfect subjunctive after «si» and conditional afterwards.
b12.pregunta: You imagine it is sunny tomorrow. Which form is missing?
p.alquilara.consejo: Imperfect subjunctive of «alquilar»: from «alquilaron», «-ron» becomes «-ra». It follows «si».
p.estuviera.consejo: Imperfect subjunctive of «estar»: from «estuvieron», «-ron» becomes «-ra». «Si estuviera en tu lugar…»
p.iría.consejo: Conditional of «ir»: regular, «ir» + «ía». The «í» is stressed. «Me iría» means I would leave.
p.aceptara.consejo: Imperfect subjunctive of «aceptar»: from «aceptaron», «-ron» becomes «-ra». It follows «si».
p.fácil.consejo: It has no feminine form: «un plan fácil», «una tarea fácil». The plural is «fáciles».
p.hicieras.consejo: Imperfect subjunctive of «hacer» with «tú»: from «hicieron», «hiciera» → «hicieras». The «h» is silent.
p.irías.consejo: Conditional of «ir» with «tú»: «ir» + «ías». The «í» is stressed.
p.pudieras.consejo: Imperfect subjunctive of «poder» with «tú»: from «pudieron», «pudiera» → «pudieras». After «si».
p.ayudarías.consejo: Conditional of «ayudar» with «tú»: the whole infinitive plus «-ías». It goes in the result part.
p.iríamos.consejo: Conditional of «ir» with «nosotros»: «ir» + «íamos». The accent mark is on the «í».
p.patio.consejo: It is masculine: «el patio». The «io» is one syllable: «PA-tyo».
p.ladrillo.consejo: It is masculine: «el ladrillo». «De ladrillo» describes what something is made of. The «ll» sounds like «y».
p.extiende.consejo: It comes from «extender»: the «e» becomes «ie» in «extiendo», «extiendes», «extiende». The «x» sounds «ks».
p.ruta.consejo: It is feminine: «la ruta». The initial «r» sounds strong: «RRU-ta».
p.lentos.consejo: It is the masculine plural of «lento», agreeing with «trenes». The opposite is «rápidos».
p.dispone.consejo: It comes from «disponer», conjugated like «poner». It takes «de»: «disponer de dos semanas».
p.semanas.consejo: It is the plural of «la semana». The «s» is the same in singular and plural.
p.cruzaría.consejo: Conditional of «cruzar»: the whole infinitive plus «-ía». The «z» sounds «th» in Spain.
p.cubiertas.consejo: It is the feminine plural of «cubierto», agreeing with «montañas». It takes «de»: «cubiertas de nieve».
p.empañadas.consejo: It comes from «empañar». It agrees with «ventanas». Do not confuse it with «empanadas» (pastries).
p.dormiría.consejo: Conditional of «dormir»: the whole infinitive plus «-ía». The «o» does not change here.
p.alojamiento.consejo: It is masculine: «el alojamiento». It comes from «alojar». The «j» sounds like «h».
p.sencillo.consejo: It changes with gender: «sencillo», «sencilla». The «c» before «i» sounds «th»; the «ll» sounds «y».
p.lago.consejo: It is masculine: «el lago». The «g» before «o» sounds hard.
p.despertaría.consejo: Conditional of «despertar»: the whole infinitive plus «-ía». «La despertaría»: «la» is the person woken.
p.suavidad.consejo: It ends in «-dad» and is feminine: «la suavidad». «Con suavidad» means gently.
p.escribiría.consejo: Conditional of «escribir»: the whole infinitive plus «-ía». Its participle is irregular: «escrito».
p.largas.consejo: It is the feminine plural of «largo». Here it goes before the noun: «largas cartas».
p.cartas.consejo: It is the plural of «la carta». «Carta» also means a menu or a playing card.
p.cafés.consejo: It is the plural of «el café». The accent mark stays: «cafés». It means both the drink and the place.
p.llenos.consejo: It is the masculine plural of «lleno», agreeing with «cafés». It takes «de»: «llenos de voces».
p.voces.consejo: It is the plural of «la voz»: the final «z» becomes «c» before «-es».
p.extrañas.consejo: It is the feminine plural of «extraño». Here it means unfamiliar. The «ñ» sounds like «ny».
p.volver.consejo: With «al»: «al volver» means when returning. The «o» becomes «ue» in the present: «vuelvo».
p.marcas.consejo: It is the plural of «la marca». «Marca» is also a brand: «una marca de ropa».
p.manchas.consejo: It is the plural of «la mancha». The «ch» is like English «ch». «Manchas de café» are coffee stains.
